einzeiler: Raine Maida discusses three decades of turning pain into music and finding purpose.
kurzfassung: Raine Maida reflects on how discovering Peter Gabriel and rock music as a teenager provided a lifeline during his parents' divorce. He discusses the creative process behind Our Lady Peace, the vulnerability required for songwriting, and his collaborative documentary with his wife. Additionally, he highlights his humanitarian work with War Child and explains how music continues to sustain him daily.
stichpunkte: Attending an early Peter Gabriel concert shifted his perspective on music having a purposeful global platform.
Parental divorce and a disliked boarding school led him to immerse himself in lyrics and records as a form of religion.
Adopting the name Rain marked his transition from a struggling teenager into an artist.
Early albums like Naveed were recorded during late-night studio sessions before signing a record deal.
The song 4AM established the importance of radical vulnerability in connecting with listeners.
Making the 2019 documentary I'm Gonna Break Your Heart captured the raw, difficult process of writing music with his wife, Chantal Kreviazuk.
He does not write songs when he is happy, relying instead on exploring turmoil and curiosity.
He remains a passionate supporter of War Child, witnessing firsthand their impactful work supporting affected children.

clips.hook: Peter Gabriel and a global view of music
clips.text: Attending a Peter Gabriel concert exposed him to socially conscious artistry that addressed global issues rather than just providing pure entertainment.

clips.hook: Recording late-night sessions on a tight budget
clips.text: The band had to wait until regular studio sessions ended at midnight so they could sneak in and record through the early morning hours.

clips.hook: Never writing a song while happy
clips.text: He explains that he exclusively turns to instruments when dealing with personal turmoil or curiosity, never during periods of happiness.

clips.hook: Freezing on an isolated island in January
clips.text: Seeking a remote place to write without distractions led them to an empty island where all the residents had left for the winter.
Visiting Afghanistan offered firsthand proof of how effectively organizations protect children who bear no responsibility for local conflicts.

beschreibung:
[Encore] Raine Maida — the voice of Our Lady Peace — has spent three decades turning personal struggle into songs that have saved countless listeners. In this conversation with Lynn Hoffman, Raine traces his path from a life-changing Peter Gabriel concert to writing Naveed as a teenager processing his parents’ divorce, and opens up about the vulnerability behind Clumsy‘s “4am.” He also shares the story behind I’m Gonna Break Your Heart, the documentary and album he made with his wife and songwriting partner Chantal Kreviazuk, and reflects on why — 30 years in — music still saves him every single day.
